question_text: When a positive leap second is added to Coordinated Universal Time, how is the added second normally labeled?
correct_answer: The added second is labeled 23:59:60 before the clock advances to 00:00:00.
incorrect_answer: The added second is labeled 23:59:59 before the clock advances to 00:00:00.
source_name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
ground_truth_note: NIST describes a positive leap second as an added second shown as 23:59:60 before the next day begins at 00:00:00.

question_text: Where is the geographic center of the United States when all 50 states are included?
correct_answer: It is near Belle Fourche, South Dakota, when all 50 states are included.
incorrect_answer: It is near Lebanon, Kansas, when all 50 states are included.
source_citation: USGS, Where is the geographic center of the United States?
ground_truth_note: USGS identifies the geographic center of the 50 states as near Belle Fourche, South Dakota, and distinguishes it from the conterminous U.S. center near Lebanon, Kansas.

question_text: Under the formal astronomical definition, what condition keeps Pluto in the dwarf planet category rather than the planet category?
correct_answer: It meets the roundness condition, but it has not cleared the neighborhood around its orbit.
incorrect_answer: It meets the orbital-clearing condition, but it has not achieved a nearly round shape.
source_citation: IAU, Pluto and the Developing Landscape of Our Solar System
ground_truth_note: The IAU definition classifies Pluto as a dwarf planet because it orbits the Sun and is nearly round but has not cleared the neighborhood around its orbit.

question_text: In metric measurement, how many square meters are in one hectare?
correct_answer: One hectare is equal to 10,000 square meters.
incorrect_answer: One hectare is equal to 1,000 square meters.
source_name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
source_citation: NIST, Guide for the Use of the International System of Units, Chapter 5
ground_truth_note: NIST lists the hectare as a unit outside the SI that is equal to 10,000 square meters.

question_text: What subject does the Twenty-Seventh Amendment to the U.S. Constitution address?
correct_answer: It delays changes to congressional compensation until after an election for the House of Representatives has occurred.
incorrect_answer: It delays changes to presidential compensation until after an election for the House of Representatives has occurred.
ground_truth_note: The Twenty-Seventh Amendment states that laws varying compensation for Senators and Representatives do not take effect until an election of Representatives has intervened.

question_text: In climate terminology, what ocean condition defines El Niño?
correct_answer: It is unusually warm surface water in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean.
incorrect_answer: It is unusually cool surface water in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean.
ground_truth_note: NOAA describes El Niño as unusually warm ocean temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific.

question_text: At the federal level, what is the general failure-to-file penalty when a taxpayer files a required federal tax return late and tax is unpaid?
correct_answer: The penalty is generally 5% of the unpaid tax for each month or part of a month the return is late, up to 25%.
incorrect_answer: The penalty is generally 0.5% of the unpaid tax for each month or part of a month the return is late, up to 25%.
ground_truth_note: The IRS states that the failure-to-file penalty is generally 5% of unpaid taxes for each month or part of a month a return is late, capped at 25%.

question_text: At the federal level, how long does a qualified beneficiary generally have to elect COBRA continuation coverage after receiving an election notice or losing coverage, whichever is later?
correct_answer: The qualified beneficiary generally has at least 60 days, measured from the later of the election notice or loss of coverage, to elect COBRA.
incorrect_answer: The qualified beneficiary generally has at least 30 days, measured from the later of the election notice or loss of coverage, to elect COBRA.
source_citation: DOL, Continuation of Health Coverage: COBRA
ground_truth_note: The Department of Labor states that qualified beneficiaries must be given an election period of at least 60 days to choose COBRA continuation coverage.

question_text: At the federal level, if a notice of deficiency is addressed to a taxpayer within the United States, how long does the taxpayer generally have to petition the Tax Court?
correct_answer: The taxpayer generally has 90 days from the date the notice of deficiency was mailed to file a Tax Court petition.
incorrect_answer: The taxpayer generally has 60 days from the date the notice of deficiency was mailed to file a Tax Court petition.
ground_truth_note: The IRS explains that a taxpayer generally has 90 days from the notice date to petition the Tax Court after a notice of deficiency.

question_text: At the federal level, how soon must a written credit-card billing-error dispute generally reach the creditor after the first bill containing the error was sent?
correct_answer: The written dispute generally must reach the creditor within 60 days after the first bill containing the error was sent.
incorrect_answer: The written dispute generally must reach the creditor within 90 days after the first bill containing the error was sent.
ground_truth_note: The FTC states that a billing-error notice must reach the creditor within 60 days after the first bill with the error was sent.

question_text: At the federal level, what is the general hours-worked requirement for an employee to be eligible for FMLA leave with a covered employer?
correct_answer: The employee generally must have worked at least 1,250 hours during the 12 months before the FMLA leave starts.
incorrect_answer: The employee generally must have worked at least 1,000 hours during the 12 months before the FMLA leave starts.
source_citation: DOL Fact Sheet #28, The Family and Medical Leave Act
ground_truth_note: The Department of Labor lists 1,250 hours of service during the 12 months before leave as one of the employee eligibility requirements for FMLA leave.

question_text: At the federal level, for someone born from 1951 through 1959 with a traditional IRA, at what age do required minimum distributions generally have to begin?
correct_answer: Required minimum distributions generally begin for that person at age 73.
incorrect_answer: Required minimum distributions generally begin for that person at age 72.
source_citation: IRS, Retirement Plan and IRA Required Minimum Distributions FAQs
ground_truth_note: The IRS required minimum distribution FAQs state that account owners born in 1951 through 1959 generally use age 73 for the required beginning age.
